summary: Listed as Wolf Ridge at Roan High Knob's coordinates; CCC built a fire tower there in 1933. Now a former lookout site with footings.

facts.status_note: Former lookout site; photo captions label lookout footings.

access.note: Reached on foot from the Appalachian Trail; the site page gives a 0.2-mile detour with a 120-foot climb.

visit.trail_note: Blue-blazed side trail from the Appalachian Trail; about five minutes to the top.

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps built a fire tower and fire warden's cabin on Roan High Knob.
Cabin renovated and became the Roan High Knob Shelter for Appalachian Trail hikers.

evidence.supports: Tower list calls the site Wolf Ridge at 36.10447, -82.12240, Mitchell-Carter, with a note reading roanhigh knob
1933 CCC construction of the Roan Mountain Fire Tower and a fire wardens cabin
evidence.quote: In 1933, the Civilian Conservation Corps constructed the Roan Mountain Fire Tower and a fire wardens cabin at the base.

evidence.supports: Tower impractical for spotting fires, often above the clouds; little use
evidence.quote: The fire tower was not used for an extended time because it proved to be impractical for spotting fires, very often too high above the clouds on cloudy days.

evidence.supports: Cabin renovated in 1980 and became the Roan High Knob Shelter
evidence.quote: In 1980, the cabin was renovated and became the Roan High Knob Shelter for Appalachian Trail hikers.

evidence.supports: Site listed as a former lookout
Photo captions label lookout footings and a former lookout location
Access by 0.2-mile detour from the AT with a 120-foot gain
evidence.quote: AT Access: 0.2 mile detour trail, with 120 foot gain

evidence.supports: Blue-blaze side trail reaches the top in about five minutes
evidence.quote: A blue blaze trail goes up around 5 minutes to the top.

evidence.supports: 1933 CCC built a fire tower and fire warden's cabin at the summit of Roan High Knob
evidence.quote: In 1933, the Civilian Conservation Corps constructed a fire tower and fire warden's cabin at the summit of Roan High Knob.

evidence.supports: Tower proved ineffective and did not last long
evidence.quote: Although the tower proved ineffective and did not last long

evidence.supports: Mountain straddles the North Carolina and Tennessee state line
evidence.quote: straddling the North Carolina / Tennessee state line

evidence.supports: Roan High Knob summit coordinates (GNIS-based, per Wikipedia)
1980 cabin renovated; now the Roan High Knob Shelter
evidence.quote: the cabin was renovated in 1980 and now serves as the Roan High Knob Shelter

evidence.supports: TopoQuest's Wolf Ridge is a different feature in Mitchell County
evidence.quote: Wolf Ridge is a ridge located in Mitchell County, NC

corrections.why: The tower list's coordinates (36.10447, -82.12240) match the Wikipedia coordinates for Roan High Knob (36.1045729, -82.1223004), and the list's own note reads roanhigh knob. TopoQuest places Wolf Ridge at a different spot, 4,445 ft in Mitchell County.
The site page calls it a former lookout and captions show lookout footings. No source describes a standing tower.

notes_for_editor: The record name Wolf Ridge comes from the tnlandforms list, but its coordinates and note match Roan High Knob, where the CCC built a fire tower in 1933. Name correction left for a human to decide. The 1933 date is from two sources; WillhiteWeb's cabin placement ('at the base') reads ambiguously against Wikipedia's 'at the summit'; the story avoids the placement. A search snippet dated the cabin to 1934 (tehcc.org), not read, not used. No source found gives a removal date for the tower. Footings are evidenced only by photo captions on one site page.
